title: Merlin: Multi-tier Optimization of eBPF Code for Performance and Compactness
problem: eBPF programs face strict instruction count constraints in the Linux kernel, and existing compilers fail to identify and exploit key optimization opportunities, resulting in suboptimal performance and code that may exceed kernel limits.
motivation: eBPF is critical for kernel observability, performance monitoring, and security in production Linux systems, making efficient compilation essential for wide adoption.
method: Merlin optimizes eBPF programs (which run in the Linux kernel under strict instruction count limits) by transforming their code after initial compilation but before kernel verification. It uses two optimization techniques: instruction merging, which combines multiple operations into fewer, more efficient ones; and strength reduction, which replaces expensive operations with cheaper equivalents that produce the same result.
key_novelty: The core idea is using compiler techniques specifically tailored to eBPF (custom compiler passes and bytecode rewriting) to discover optimization opportunities that general-purpose compilers overlook.
contributions: Merlin optimization framework combining LLVM passes and bytecode rewriting for eBPF programs
Instruction merging and strength reduction techniques optimized for kernel ISA constraints
73% instruction count reduction and 60% runtime overhead reduction across diverse eBPF workloads
